summary:
[  edit  ]
The Audio Device In  CHOP  receives audio from any of the attached audio input devices using DirectSound/CoreAudio or ASIO. It always outputs time sliced audio data.
If you want to capture the data in memory, use a  Trail CHOP  or  Record CHOP .	If you want to record to a file, use  Audio File Out CHOP  or  Movie File Out TOP .
The Audio Device In  CHOP  can receive analog control voltages ( CVs ) as long as your audio device's analog to digital converters can handle constant non-zero voltages.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Turns the audio input on or off.

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between default DirectSound/CoreAudio, ASIO, or native device supported drivers.

parameters.label: DirectSound/CoreAudio

parameters.description: The default Windows audio driver (a.k.a. WDM) or macOS CoreAudio driver, depending on your OS.

parameters.label: ASIO
parameters.name: asio
parameters.description: Low-latency drivers which usually come from the hardware's manufacturer.

parameters.label: DataPath (RGBEASY)

parameters.description: Native support for capturing the audio from DataPath devices.

parameters.label: Blackmagic
parameters.name: blackmagic
parameters.description: Native support for capturing the audio from  Blackmagic Design  devices.

parameters.label: AJA

parameters.description: Native support for capturing the audio from  AJA  devices.

parameters.label: Device
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: A menu of available audio devices to receive input from. Selecting  default  sets the audio device to that which is selected in Windows  Control Panel >Sounds and Audio Devices>Audio>Sound Recording.

parameters.label: Error if Missing
parameters.name: errormissing
parameters.description: The  CHOP  will error if the specified device is not found.

parameters.label: Inputs
parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: When Driver is set to ASIO on Windows or CoreAudio on macOS, this parameter lets you pick which input channels to use.

parameters.label: Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - When Driver is set to DirectSound, this set mono, stereo, or multi-channel. Also determines how many channels are created 1(mono) or 2(stereo left and stereo right), or when set to multi-channel set the number of channels active on the Input 1 and Input 2 parameter pages.
